items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 9% in extended trading on Nov 11 as investors weighed reports that the company may move without CEO Jensen Huang. A New York Times report cited a personal relationship, and a Wall Street Journal report said Nvidia’s board is preparing to oust him; he admitted an affair with an alleged Chinese spy over the weekend. Other AI-linked stocks also declined.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Falls on Speculation Over Jensen Huang's Future

items.summary: China's Alibaba Group said on Tuesday its chip unit T-Head had confidentially filed for a Hong Kong initial public offering, advancing a spin-off that would give investors direct exposure to one of the group's key AI and chip assets. The company added details such as deal size remain undetermined and the listing remains subject to regulatory approvals.
items.title: Alibaba's T-Head Confidentially Files for Hong Kong IPO

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang after multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected of spying for China. Shares fell 8% in extended trading as the company declined to comment.
items.title: Nvidia board reportedly preparing to oust Jensen Huang

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The report cited people familiar with the matter and said the board could meet as soon as Wednesday. Earlier, the New York Times reported an affair with a company executive. Nvidia did not respond immediately; its shares fell about 8% in after-hours trading.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang Over Affairs

items.summary: On 11th November 2026, Google joined Jev and OpenAI in the decision model category with Gemini Decision 1. The API handles text, images, audio, video and PDFs, supports yes/no, choice and rubric-scoring questions, costs 10 cents per million input tokens with free output, and returns probabilities rather than flat answers.
items.title: Google's Gemini Decision 1 joins decision-model rivals

items.summary: Semafor reported that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO and founder Jensen Huang as soon as today, following media reports detailing a second extramarital affair. The board briefed the White House on its plans, per a senior administration official. Nvidia stock fell more than 8% in after-hours trading, hitting a 52-week low.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang Amid Spy Allegations

items.summary: A CBS News reporter said Nvidia's board is preparing to discuss the future of CEO Jensen Huang, with the Trump administration aware of plans to remove him. Reports cite alleged extramarital relationships, one involving a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of links to Chinese services. Huang acknowledged infidelity in a letter and apologized.
items.title: Nvidia Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Amid China-Link Allegations

items.summary: Jensen Huang, Nvidia's co-founder and CEO, admitted in a public message to employees that he had an affair with his wife of 40 years. The scandal intensified after reports linked him romantically to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive suspected by U.S. officials of being a Chinese spy feeding information to Beijing. Following the revelation, Nvidia's board reportedly prepared to oust Huang and his shares fell roughly 8% in after-hours trading on November 11, 2026. Three Republican congressmen requested a closed-door briefing about national security concerns.
items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Admits Infidelity Amid Spy Allegations and Board Ouster Reports

items.summary: This Databricks post explains how credential-driven attacks unfold and can be detected using verbose audit logs and Genie. It states that once an adversary obtains a leaked session cookie, personal access token, or service-principal credential, the breach is effectively complete because they operate under the guise of a legitimate identity. The article groups such activity into six stages—initial access, reconnaissance, harvesting credentials, establishing code execution, creating persistence, and data collection—with each stage rarely occurring in sequence. It claims that five or more distinct discovery APIs called within one minute suggests automated mapping rather than manual navigation.
items.title: Databricks Explains Detecting Credential-Driven Attacks on Its Platform

items.summary: The article explains that debt mutual funds invest in fixed-income instruments such as government securities, treasury bills and corporate bonds, aiming for relatively stable returns with lower risk than equity. It outlines risks including interest-rate and credit exposure, how investment horizon shapes fund choice, and why September outflows were driven by liquidity needs rather than shifting appetite.
items.title: What investors should know before buying debt mutual funds

items.summary: Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran calls Nvidia an amazing company but a bad investment, cautioning investors against confusing great companies with great investments. His views appear in 'The India Opportunity' by Shrishti Sahu, which examines India's growth prospects and long-term wealth creation.
items.title: Damodaran Warns Nvidia Is a Bad Investment Despite Its Strength

items.summary: An analysis by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA) found that missing PM2.5 data from monitoring stations during Diwali night in New Delhi could have raised the city's average pollution level by 49%. CREA conducted a sensitivity exercise assigning the upper measurement limit of 1,000 g/m³ to 255 missing observations out of 1,416 expected station-hours. Under this scenario, the pooled average PM2.5 concentration would have risen from 269 g/m³ to 400 g/m³.
items.title: Complete data could've raised average Diwali pollution level 49%

items.summary: Chief minister Yogi Adityanath defended bursting firecrackers during Diwali, saying he personally took part in celebrations in Ayodhya and argued that pollution concerns were being selectively raised. The remarks came on Wednesday as a senior assistant editor with TOI covering politics and governance in UP reported the statement.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Defends Diwali Firecrackers Amid Pollution Concerns

items.summary: Nigeria's President Bola Ahmed Tinubu launched his 'From Reform to Prosperity' manifesto, promising 6% annual economic growth by 2031 (s4059-4061), extra security personnel and affordable housing ahead of the January 2027 election (date-515-519). Tracka's Joshua Osiyemi notes reforms have been painful, with fuel prices rising as families struggle on 10,000 naira a day (quantity-1559-1571), while imported rice costs jumped 184% between May 2023 and October 2025 (quantity-1781-1785). Though inflation eased to 14% in September 2026 from a 34% peak, SBM Intelligence's Ikenna Okonkwo warns household costs remain high. Analysts say the opposition must unite and Tinubu must rebuild voter trust (claim-7011-7162).
items.title: Tinubu's re-election pledges face a trust deficit amid cost of living crisis

items.summary: Beau Lamarre-Condon admitted in the New South Wales Supreme Court that he threw Jesse Baird’s phone off Tom Uglys Bridge to destroy evidence, after allegedly murdering him. The former police officer is accused of fatally shooting Baird and Luke Davies on 19 February 2024. He pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
items.title: Defendant admits destroying murder victim’s phone

items.summary: Scott Colom defeated incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith, becoming the first Black senator elected from Mississippi since Reconstruction and the party’s largest midterm gain with at least 55 seats. The Associated Press called it after more than a week of counting. Hyde-Smith conceded but vowed to keep representing voters; Colom pledged to represent all Mississippians. Democrats cited national anger at Trump’s administration and efforts to redraw Black-majority districts as motivating factors, while Colom campaigned on the promise “Mississippi matters”.
items.title: Democrat Scott Colom Defeats Incumbent in Mississippi Senate Race

items.summary: Groupama Immobilier is converting Le Diamant, a nine-storey La Défense office building where about 1,800 people work (quantity-489-501), into upmarket flats. Paris La Défense plans to convert up to a fifth of the district's offices (place-895-911). Falling demand since Covid and rising vacancy rates drive the shift; Pierre-Yves Guice says diversifying office landscapes is needed to retain companies. Ludovic Delaisse notes Parisian office demand has fallen by almost a third over five to six years, while London conversion projects are 60% higher than pre-Covid levels (quantity-4482-4485). Roland Cubin warns France's tax policy could determine whether it converts just 2% or between 18 and 23% of vacant offices.
items.title: Paris office buildings converted into apartments amid falling demand

items.summary: Scott Colom won the US Senate race in Mississippi, becoming the first Black person from the state elected to the Senate in over 140 years. He edged incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by a narrow margin: 49.2% versus 48.7%, with an independent taking 2.1%. The Democratic majority rose to 55 seats as voters expressed frustration with Trump's economic policies.
items.title: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race

items.summary: A government-commissioned review by Alan Milburn is expected to recommend moving under-25s off the main sickness and disability benefits, per The Times. Many claimants could receive less as reforms are set to enter legislation next year. Neet rates among 18-to-24-year-olds rose 3% in a recent period.
items.title: Milburn Review Proposes Cutting Benefits for Young Claimants

items.summary: A new study published Wednesday in the journal Nature suggests climate change may threaten cacti more than previously thought, according to researchers who integrated spatial drought data with climate models. They found that more than a quarter of nearly 1,000 analyzed species could lose most suitable habitat by century’s end—more than 80 percent overall (s6)—far exceeding estimates based on temperature and precipitation alone. The work challenges the assumption that cacti thrive in warming conditions, as co-author Brian Enquist noted (s9). Impacts are worst in hotspots like Chile, Argentina and Central America (s11), while some regions saw modest gains offset by losses elsewhere.
items.title: Study Warns Cacti Face Heat and Drought Threat

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday (Nov 11) that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang after two extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The New York Times earlier said the affair involved executive Kimberly Powell. Reuters could not immediately verify the reports. Nvidia did not respond; its shares fell about 8 per cent in after-hours trading and it lost more than US$300 billion since news broke.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang Over Affairs

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for 33 years. Sources told the newspaper that the board is meeting soon to determine his future. Nvidia stock fell about 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday and down about 11% over five days amid Huang's scandal. Bloomberg reports Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates who could replace him as CEO.
items.title: Nvidia Stock Falls as Board Weighs Ousting Jensen Huang Amid Scandal

items.summary: Reuters reported that a Chinese university with military ties obtained Nvidia’s most powerful chips last month despite being on a US blacklist, revealing holes in Washington’s regulatory framework. Lawmakers are pressuring the Trump administration over its Megaspeed investigation amid reports of delays blacklisting the Singapore firm suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China. Semafor argued Beijing will “scale faster than the US,” weakening Nvidia.
items.title: Nvidia leak exposes US chip-control gaps

items.summary: Global index provider MSCI announced on Nov 9 that it will remove Indonesian company Barito Pacific from its indexes, effective after trading closes on Nov 30. The move comes amid a downgrade threat and reflects foreign investors pulling US$5.4 billion out of the market in 2026 as Indonesia’s benchmark fell over 40%.
items.title: MSCI Removes Barito Pacific From Its Indexes

items.summary: Alasdair Anderson describes a typical week for a Lead Solutions Architect at Databricks, balancing coding with coaching colleagues and partnering on business cases. He joined after two decades in financial services, having known the company since 2014. In just 12 months, tools like Agentbricks transformed their work from optimizing to redesigning processes. Anderson highlights customer-focused preparation and cross-time-zone collaboration as central to his role.
items.title: Databricks Introduces Alasdair Anderson as Lead Solutions Architect

items.summary: A report by His Majesty's Inspectorate of Constabulary (HMICFRS) found retrospective facial recognition is beset by errors and bias, risking wrongful arrest especially of ethnic minorities when inaccurate data is treated as evidence. Investigators sometimes lacked corroborative enquiries before acting on matches.
items.title: Police watchdog warns facial recognition risks wrongful arrests of minorities

items.summary: Marktechpost has launched GPU Leaderboard, a free cloud GPU price comparison for AI inference teams running on-demand workloads. The v1 app ranks 201 live offers from 24 providers by $/GPU-hour and includes a cost calculator that prices full runs including idle time at utilization. An example run of 8×H100 over 72 hours ranges from $967.68 to $3,545.28 across providers.
items.title: Marktechpost AI Launches GPU Leaderboard and Deploy It Extension

items.summary: During this year's Dhanteras-Diwali period, the industry body reported consumers bought 52 tonnes of gold worth ₹72,000 crore and 300 tonnes of silver valued at ₹5,400 crore. Purchases rose after gold prices corrected from around ₹1.8 lakh to ₹1.42 lakh per 10 grams, alongside wedding-season advance buying and pent-up demand following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's earlier appeal not to buy. C Vinod Hayagriv of C Krishniah Chetty Jewellers said consumer confidence in gold jewellery remains unshaken despite a 12-month price rise.
items.title: Indian Consumers Buy More Gold After Price Correction

items.summary: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators agreed in principle at peace talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended Wednesday after two days, to exchange prisoners of war and set the numbers on Thursday. The first negotiations in nine months came amid lingering differences over territory. Jared Kushner called it the biggest humanitarian release yet; Zelenskyy said its scope would be significant.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree Prisoner Swap as U.S. Warns Talks Stalled

items.summary: Net equity-oriented mutual fund inflows stood at ₹32,993 crore in October versus ₹38,306 crore in September, per AMFI. Smallcap funds declined 29% to ₹6,407 crore while large cap funds rose 20%; mid-cap inflows fell to ₹4,892.62 crore from ₹7,834.84 crore. Morningstar's Himanshu Srivastava attributed the moderation to cooling appetite for riskier segments amid volatility and global uncertainties.
items.title: Equity MF inflows fell 14% in October amid volatility

items.summary: President Nayib Bukele posted footage of attack helicopters firing near Port-au-Prince on Nov. 10, 2026, after requesting the address of gang leader Wilson Joseph; his operation reportedly killed as many as 20 people while Haitian police and Salvadoran troops operated alongside the U.N.-backed Gang Suppression Force. The intervention follows a deadly Oct. 18 ambush that Bukele used to justify sending roughly 2,500 troops. Haiti faces dire insecurity—almost 6,000 deaths in 2025—with fighting classified as armed conflict. Critics warn of civilian casualties and unclear command; the outcome will depend on whether Haitian institutions sustain gains after foreign forces depart.
items.title: El Salvador's Bukele Model Tested in Haiti Amid Gang Offensive

items.summary: Statistics New Zealand reported a record number of US arrivals in the 12 months through September, driven by favorable exchange rates and increased air connections. Total arrivals rose 9% to 3.74 million. China may soon overtake the US as its second-largest tourism market.
items.title: New Zealand Sees Record US Tourism Amid Weak Kiwi Dollar

items.summary: Queensland Opposition Leader Steven Miles apologised for the Best Practice Industry Conditions (BPIC) policy after a CFMEU inquiry found it inflated construction costs by at least 20 per cent across three projects. Commissioner Stuart Wood called BPIC "damaging" and described his estimate as "conservative." Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie said the government is considering reforms, including a new building code.
items.title: Queensland Labor Apologises After CFMEU Inquiry Finds BPIC Inflated Costs

items.summary: Ireland is mounting its largest security operation as around 50 European leaders gather in Dublin amid growing concerns over hybrid attacks, following a wave of hoax bomb threats targeting airlines and media organisations across Europe. Irish police reported new incidents on Monday and Tuesday.
items.title: European Leaders Convene in Dublin Amid Hybrid Threat Concerns

items.summary: Officials scuttled the SS United States on Wednesday about 25 miles southwest of Destin, Florida, to create what is billed as the world's largest artificial reef. The $13.5 million project aims to draw divers and fishing enthusiasts while providing habitat for tuna, marlin and swordfish.
items.title: Florida Sinks Historic Liner as World's Largest Artificial Reef

items.summary: Violent clashes broke out across central Barcelona shortly after a largely peaceful mass demonstration on Wednesday, 11 November, as masked protesters threw objects at police near Passeig de Gràcia and Plaça de Catalunya. Burning barricades formed while shops were damaged; riot police responded with charges. Municipal police estimated more than 55,000 took part, organisers closer to 400,000. The unrest occurred during Spain's first general strike since 2012, ahead of a snap election.
items.title: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after peaceful general strike march

items.summary: As peace talks in Abu Dhabi ended their final day, Kyiv and Moscow agreed Wednesday to a large-scale prisoner exchange described by US envoy Jared Kushner as the biggest ever, though neither side gave figures. Zelensky said Kyiv was waiting on Russia's response to a possible 1,000-for-1,000 swap that could reach 1,200 prisoners. The parties discussed security guarantees in greater detail and welcomed what Zelensky called a change in tone from the US toward Europe's inclusion in talks. Negotiators Medinsky and Arakhamia said discussion would continue before year-end, while EU officials warned of little genuine progress.
items.title: Russia and Ukraine Agree Major Prisoner Swap as Talks End

items.summary: US stocks ended the session over 1% higher, driven by AI-fueled optimism. The S&P 500 rose 96.91 points to 7,617.84 and the Nasdaq gained 398.70 points to 25,464.57. CoreWeave shares surged more than 20%, while Nvidia climbed 3.8%. Volatility eased for a fourth straight session. However, hotter-than-expected inflation data raised expectations of a December rate increase, adding uncertainty.
items.title: US stocks close higher on AI optimism as rate fears grow

items.summary: Global electric vehicle sales rose 8% in October 2026, reaching 2.09 million units worldwide (quantity-242-258), per Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Europe led with a 49% jump to 510,000 EVs (quantity-641-652), driven largely by fully electric cars up 49%, while Germany’s share topped 45%. North America posted its first year-over-year gain of 24% to 130,000 units in October (quantity-1831-1834; quantity-1853-1860), but Charles Lester of Benchmark noted the market stabilized at a lower level rather than recovering. China’s sales fell 12% year over year as its share rose to a fresh high, and other markets grew 85%. (quote-2494-2703)
items.title: Europe EV sales surge while North America rebounds cautiously

items.summary: Vast crowds braved torrential rain in Madrid's historic centre to join a general strike calling for affordable housing and better wages. Police placed attendance at approximately 120,000. The UGT and CCOO trade unions organized the stoppage ahead of the 29 November snap election. Union leaders called turnout massive but uneven; the CEOE employers' federation dismissed it as a failure.
items.title: Madrid crowds demand housing and wages amid rain

items.summary: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, becoming the state's first Black senator since 1874. The narrow victory followed several days of ballot counting after November 3 midterm elections and marks a significant political shift in a long-conservative state. US media projected his win this Wednesday.
items.title: Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Seat in Narrow Victory

items.summary: Trystar, LLC is introducing five new series of relays in a narrow 17.5mm wide DIN-rail form factor with dedicated solutions for timing, load alternation, and voltage and phase monitoring. Designed for OEMs, panel builders, and industrial users across water/wastewater management, automation, HVAC, refrigeration, petrochemical, and agriculture sectors, the portfolio aims to conserve valuable panel space while providing purpose-built functionality.
items.title: Trystar Launches Compact 17.5mm Relay Series for Control Panels

items.summary: Alexander Darchiev, Russia's ambassador to the United States, died suddenly in Moscow on Wednesday at age 66 after roughly one and a half years in office, Moscow's foreign ministry announced. The ministry described him as an outstanding diplomat, experienced leader and kind colleague but gave no further details. The US State Department confirmed his death and offered condolences.
items.title: Russia's US Ambassador Darchiev Dies at 66

items.summary: The Caribbean faces growing threats from seaweed blooms, coral bleaching and environmental pressures that endanger tourism-dependent economies. In an interview with CGTN reporter Keerqinfu, Athill Dean Jonas, Antigua and Barbuda's former minister responsible for the Blue Economy, called for greater cooperation with China in marine research and environmental protection. He said Chinese expertise could help Caribbean nations address pressing energy challenges.
items.title: Caribbean Leaders Seek China's Help on Ocean and Energy Challenges

items.summary: Alfredo Giron of the World Economic Forum's Ocean Agenda told CGTN that China is a major influence in the global ocean economy, citing figures on offshore wind capacity and port traffic. He also highlighted China's proposals to strengthen marine conservation in Antarctica and host the BBNJ Agreement secretariat, framing these as signs of leadership.
items.title: From offshore wind to ocean governance: China's growing global role

items.summary: Violent clashes broke out across central Barcelona shortly after a peaceful general strike march on Wednesday evening, with masked protesters throwing objects at police and setting up burning barricades. Municipal police estimated more than 55,000 people took part while organisers put the figure closer to 400,000. Eighteen arrests brought the day's total to 20. Catalan President Salvador Illa condemned the violence as it unfolded during Spain's first general strike since 2012.
items.title: Clashes Erupt in Barcelona After Peaceful General Strike March

items.summary: The Bombay High Court upheld a Hindu woman's right to marry a Muslim man, granting her protection after alleged family threats. The 21-year-old petitioner married on October 19, 2026 and sought safety from police who reportedly refused action before forcing her to Uttar Pradesh. Justices Advait M Sethna and Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale reaffirmed an adult woman's freedom to choose a partner irrespective of religion or caste, citing the Supreme Court's Shafin Jahan judgment under Article 21. The bench declined specific observations on police conduct while urging strict adherence to law.
items.title: Bombay High Court Upholds Woman's Right to Choose Spouse Across Religion

items.summary: ExxonMobil’s carbon capture and storage project near Cheek, a predominantly Black community outside Beaumont, Texas, received approval in September after the state won federal permitting authority. The company is preparing to inject CO2 thousands of feet underground, which could be the first operating project of its kind in Texas. Residents question whether it will keep groundwater safe, arguing they should not serve as test subjects for unproven technology. At a March hearing, Earthjustice representatives contended ExxonMobil had failed to ensure adequate safety protections. Meanwhile, Railroad Commission spokesperson Bryce Dubee defended the agency’s record on drinking water protection. The project has drawn criticism from experts who call carbon capture and storage “mostly a dangerous distraction,” while supporters emphasize its role in climate efforts.
items.title: Texas Approves ExxonMobil Carbon Storage Near Black Community

items.summary: Utilities built over 21,000 km of new transmission lines last year, the International Renewable Energy Agency reported at COP31. That is 50% more than the previous year, IRENA noted in its report. La Camera, IRENA’s director-general, said power grids are essential to raising global electrification to 35% by 2035 and that grid investment must more than double, reaching a cumulative USD 10 trillion by 2035. Wood Mackenzie added this week that countries prioritizing energy security over emission-reduction plans could achieve lower emissions through faster electrification, replacing hydrocarbon import dependence.
items.title: Global Power Grid Expansion Surges 50% to Record High

items.summary: Vast crowds flooded Madrid's streets in torrential rain during a joint UGT, CCOO and activist-group stoppage calling for affordable housing and better wages. Police put attendance at approximately 120,000; union leaders called it "massive" but noted uneven support across heavy industry, ports and coastal hubs. The CEOE employers' federation dismissed the action as a "failure", citing minimal disruption. Anger over shelter was sparked by an eviction in September.
items.title: Madrid crowds demand housing and wages amid rain

items.summary: BYD launched the second-generation Seal 07, debuting its new Cloud Carriage body control system. The EV starts at 139,900 yuan and measures 5,080 mm long with a CLTC range up to 481 miles. Zhang Zhuo of BYD’s Ocean sales division demonstrated the system in a video. It adjusts damping force across 100 to 10,000 Nm and works with road-surface LiDAR sensors.
items.title: BYD Unveils Cloud Carriage Body Control System on New Seal 07

items.summary: Procurement records show a Chinese university with deep ties to the People’s Liberation Army bought Nvidia’s powerful H200 AI chips last month despite being on a U.S. export blacklist, highlighting gaps in Washington’s efforts to curb China’s access to advanced technology. The findings come as Jensen Huang faces scrutiny over lobbying for looser restrictions.
items.title: Chinese University Bought Nvidia H200 Chips Despite U.S. Blacklist

items.summary: The Japan Fair Trade Commission approved a business improvement plan from Amazon Japan, ending an investigation into allegations it pressured sellers to lower prices. Under commitment procedures, the JFTC will monitor implementation for five years without finding a violation.
items.title: JFTC Approves Amazon Japan Plan to Ease Seller Pricing Rules

items.summary: President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday that Samsung Electronics' 6 trillion won ($4.48 billion) investment in a high-bandwidth memory chip packaging plant in Asan would be followed by about 40 trillion won in advanced equipment, using the exchange rate of $1 = 1,339.5500 won.
items.title: South Korea's Lee says Samsung chip packaging expansion to spur $30 billion additional investment

items.summary: Stock brokerage Samsung Securities launched LUMINA, a four-member AI-generated K-pop girl group whose debut video 'Override' passed 3 million YouTube views about five weeks after release. Uhm Sewon, head of the media strategy team, said finding presenters was difficult and that measurable returns were hard to quantify yet.
items.title: Samsung Securities' AI K-pop Group Draws Millions of Views

items.summary: Nvidia tumbled about 10% in late trading after CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair, prompting a board meeting on his future. Nasdaq 100 futures fell over 1% and S&P 500 contracts lost 0.5%. The crisis may reverberate across Asian markets among suppliers including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc. Strategists remain divided, with some confident the AI build-out continues.
items.title: Asian stocks mixed as Nvidia turmoil hits AI-linked shares

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday that Nvidia's board is preparing to remove CEO Jensen Huang, citing people familiar with the matter (s1). Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the meeting and declined to confirm details. Analysts offered mixed reactions: some argued the company's business fundamentals remain intact despite leadership turmoil, while others warned of share-price pressure and uncertainty around its China operations and future strategy. One strategist noted investors may see an initial negative reaction before looking elsewhere in the AI sector (s13). The report left much unresolved about timing and next steps.
items.title: Nvidia board weighs ousting Jensen Huang amid leadership uncertainty

items.summary: Days after launching its investor roadshow, Anthropic saw orders for its initial public offering surpass available shares multiple times over, putting it on track for the largest market debut in history (s0). Anchor-sized commitments from major institutional funds filled the order book despite a broader pullback in AI equities last week (s1). According to reports from Bloomberg and the Financial Times, underwriters are weighing pushing Anthropic’s target valuation beyond $1.5 trillion — up from the $1.1 trillion figure floated days ago (s2).
items.title: Anthropic’s Oversubscribed IPO May Push Valuation Past $1.5 Trillion

items.summary: Nvidia shares fell 8% in after-hours trading on Wednesday, following reports that the board was preparing to discuss whether CEO Jensen Huang should remain. The Wall Street Journal and CBS News cited unnamed sources about plans for his removal, while the New York Times reported another alleged relationship involving Nvidia vice president Kimberly Powell. Huang acknowledged one affair and apologized. A board investigation led by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz is underway.
items.title: Nvidia Shares Fall After Reports of CEO Jensen Huang's Possible Exit

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday that Nvidia's board is preparing to oust co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang amid a growing list of controversies. The New York Times reported he had a second extramarital affair with vice president Kimberly Powell, citing video evidence. He previously acknowledged a relationship with Alice Huang at Megaspeed; US intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this past spring alleging she was an asset of China's Ministry of State Security. Nvidia shareholders filed a class action lawsuit over undisclosed information.
items.title: Nvidia Board Prepares to Oust Jensen Huang Over Affairs and China Ties

items.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang, the company’s 63-year-old CEO, amid allegations of a second extramarital affair involving an executive who reports to him. The report says the board was set to meet as early as Wednesday.
items.title: Jensen Huang May Be Ousted by Nvidia Board

items.summary: Meta is making three of its Muse models available through Google Cloud for developers and businesses using the platform, per CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s announcement on X. The models now accessible are Muse Ember, Muse Spark 1.3 and Muse Wonder. This move expands options beyond Google’s own offerings as cloud platforms grow into distribution channels for AI models from different companies.
items.title: Meta AI Models Reach Google Cloud

items.summary: Demand for Anthropic’s initial public offering reportedly sold out before pricing began, driven by large anchor-size indications of interest from investors who asked not to be identified as the details are private. The company and its co-founders plan to raise up to $90.4 billion across an IPO and a private placement, which could make it the largest listing ever.
items.title: Anthropic IPO Sold Out Before Launch

items.summary: Philip Fearnside argues that President Lula must change course to protect the Amazon rainforest after narrowly avoiding a Bolsonaro administration. He warns of climate tipping points and links them to deforestation, logging and fossil fuels. The author lists policies he views as harmful: new oil and gas fields including the “Mouth of the Amazon” project, roads like BR-319 Highway paving on 14 September despite lacking IBAMA license, subsidies for pasture and soy conversion, land tenure regularization legalizing illegal claims, and unsustainable forest management. He cites figures such as 1.6 million hectares in Lula’s campaign platform concessions and a fine of R$292 million (US$59 million) from deforestation in 2023. The piece is commentary that does not represent Mongabay’s views.
items.title: Lula’s Amazon Policies Threaten Forest Survival

items.summary: The article is an opinion piece by Merve Hickok, Marc Rotenberg, Ren Bin Lee Dixon and Idil I. Kaner of the Center for AI and Digital Policy (CAIDP), published Nov 11, 2026. It argues that selecting the next UN Secretary-General matters greatly for global AI governance as António Guterres steps down after a decade in office. The piece reviews frameworks produced under Guterres, including the 2021 UNESCO Recommendation and reports by Michelle Bachelet and CAIDP’s HLAB-AI body. It notes that the United States and China rejected new UN-level AI rules while pursuing bilateral arrangements, and flags the July 2026 OpenAI-Hugging Face incidents as a control concern. The authors urge leadership grounded in human rights and recommend selecting a woman for the first time. Published Nov 11, 2026.
items.title: UN Leaders Debate AI Governance as New Secretary-General Is Chosen

items.summary: The Supreme Court collegium is developing a well-defined policy framework for transferring high court judges, moving away from informal methods based on integrity, expertise or closeness to an ex-CJI. The five-member panel led by CJI Surya Kant discussed discarding random transfers and factoring in reconsideration of unimplemented recommendations. Past transfers were often seen as punitive over the past five years.
items.title: Supreme Court Collegium Seeks Streamlined Judge Transfer Policy

items.summary: A three-storey building collapsed in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York City. According to reports from the ground, two people have died and several others were injured when the structure fell. Rescuers are searching for survivors trapped under the rubble. Footage shows exposed bedrooms and stairwells in an adjacent building following the collapse.
items.title: Building Collapse in New York Kills Two and Injures Several

items.summary: A three-story building in Brooklyn’s Flatbush section collapsed Wednesday near a construction site, killing at least two people and trapping others beneath the wreckage. Firefighters were called around 4pm and searched through debris by hand with rescue dogs, drones and saws. Officials said two died and four more arrived critically injured; seven patients were children, twelve were stable, and one firefighter had minor injuries.
items.title: Brooklyn Building Collapse Kills at Least Two

items.summary: A proposal by Neil Francey suggests Australian state governments could sue tobacco companies for up to $50bn in public hospital and healthcare costs, targeting British American Tobacco (BAT), Philip Morris and Imperial Brands. South Australia is seeking advice on the plan; other states are reviewing it. The proposal argues firms should bear decades of misleading conduct under consumer law. Blair Boyer called there a “substantial” public interest but stressed due diligence. Laura Hunter said companies should cover harm costs. Francey noted litigation would require enabling legislation and well-resourced outside law firms, warning suits could otherwise fail on procedural grounds.
items.title: Australian States Could Sue Tobacco Firms Over Healthcare Costs

items.summary: The rupee closed at about 93.69 per dollar, roughly 24 paise stronger than the previous close of 93.93 (quantity-20-28, quantity-65-70), aided by broad-based dollar selling and an increase in the dollar index from 101.8 to 102.5 (quantity-646-651, quantity-655-667). The Reserve Bank of India earlier announced measures to curb speculative activity as the currency approached a 97-per-dollar mark (quantity-890-892). Bhansali expects 93.50 as support (quantity-306-311), while another analyst cites 93.40 (quantity-494-499); the rupee is expected to stay within a range of 93.25 to 94.00 on Thursday, with 93.25 as the lower bound (quantity-958-963).
items.title: Indian Rupee Reaches Near Seven-Month High Against Dollar

items.summary: An op-ed by the team behind My Octopus Teacher argues kelp forests need their own identity in conservation frameworks, unlike coral reefs and mangroves. The authors note less than 2% of kelp forests are meaningfully protected (quantity-1774-1776), warning warming waters could wipe out up to 25 million hectares by 2050 (quantity-1851-1870, date-1916-1920). A 2023 policy brief found kelp forests receive the least global attention: cited 43 times versus coral reefs at 38 and mangroves at 43 in international law (quantity-3700-3708, quantity-3722-3730). The piece points to initiatives like the Kelp Forest Challenge, aiming to restore 2.5 million acres by 2040 (quantity-6321-6338, date-6414-6418), and calls for official recognition and a dedicated awareness day.
items.title: Op-ed Urges Naming Kelp Forests Like Coral Reefs

items.summary: Delhi is set to inaugurate its longest Chhath Ghat, an nearly 11-km-long stretch along the Munak Canal near Singalpur village in North Delhi. BJP national president Nitin Nabin will open it on Thursday for Chhath Puja (November 13-16). The government released water from the Haiderpur Water Treatment Plant to ensure a clean flow, removed about 1,400 truckloads of debris, and installed CCTV cameras, permanent steps and toilets. Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said devotees can reach the ghats without difficulty.
items.title: Delhi Unveils Longest Chhath Ghat Along Munak Canal Today

items.summary: The last Tasmanian-brewed James Boag beer sold for $1,300. Local production has ceased; all James Boag beer will now be brewed on the mainland after 2024. Former worker Sam Cox owns it and plans no sale. The Launceston brewery closes after 145 years amid a long-term decline in Australia's beer market.
items.title: Tasmanian brewery's final beer sells at auction

items.summary: Two Australian Federal Police officers and their families left Türkiye after safety concerns arose while targeting high-profile fugitives, per a statement tendered in Masood Zakaria's court case. Superintendent Marie Andersson said AFP received information raising security worries at Ankara Post, prompting relocation for six weeks until measures were implemented. The disclosure emerged during Zakaria's challenge to his 2023 deportation.
items.title: AFP Officers Relocated After Crime-Boss Safety Threats

items.summary: The Uttarakhand government transferred 10 IAS and 20 PCS officers in a statewide reshuffle, the item states. The changes affect district administration and roles in tourism, urban development and Panchayati Raj departments. Several chief development officers, additional district magistrates and municipal commissioners were reassigned across districts including Dehradun, Pithoragarh, Almora, Roorkee and Uttarkashi.
items.title: Uttarakhand Transfers 30 Officers in Bureaucratic Reshuffle

items.summary: Three CRPF personnel were injured when two heavily armed terrorists opened fire on a Central Reserve Police Force checkpost near Mir Bazar in Kashmir's Kulgam district on Wednesday, one critically. The attackers approached the post on foot from about 50 metres away and fled through forested cover; ground verification ruled out motorcycle involvement. A Motorola phone and SIM card were recovered. Officials said security forces' prompt response thwarted the attack before heavy casualties occurred. Suspected link to Mohammed Lateef Bhat of Lashkar-e-Taiba is under investigation.
items.title: Terrorists Fire at CRPF Checkpost in Kulgam

items.summary: The Haryana government is intensifying efforts against stubble burning, reporting 206 farm fires across 23 districts this season. It has distributed agricultural machinery and offered subsidies of up to 50 per cent plus Rs 1,200 per acre incentives. About Rs 500 crore will be disbursed under the scheme, while fines totalling Rs 3.55 lakh were imposed through 62 challans. The state is combining technology-based monitoring with enforcement measures.
items.title: Haryana Cracks Down on Farm Fires Amid Stubble-Burning Season

items.summary: The Associated Press reported that Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, making him Mississippi's first Black US senator since Reconstruction after a prolonged ballot count. The result was framed as part of a broader midterm rebuke of Donald Trump and signaled Democratic momentum in the South. Party leaders including Chuck Schumer praised Colom, while Hyde-Smith conceded online. Analysts noted strong turnout in majority-Black counties but pointed out that Mississippi had shifted leftward from 2024, when Trump won it by nearly 23 points.
items.title: Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Seat in Historic Upset

items.summary: The Union Cabinet extended the Stand-Up India and Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana credit guarantee schemes for five years, allocating ₹4,111 crore to the Stand-Up India fund (quantity-341-347) and ₹5,000 crore to the Micro Units fund under PMMY (quantity-386-392). The government said guarantees will cover loans up to ₹1 crore for greenfield enterprises by women and SC/ST entrepreneurs. Guarantee fees are set at 0.50% annually with an 85% guarantee cover, while Mudra support is expected to reach ₹12.60 lakh crore (quantity-1215-1221).
items.title: Union Cabinet Extends Stand-Up India and Mudra Schemes

items.summary: Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan addressed students at V.O. Chidambaram College's platinum jubilee, calling India's unity essential to protecting its diverse cultures and domestic market. He urged nationalism over fragmentation, which could leave smaller nations vulnerable. On language, he encouraged learning multiple languages while opposing anti-Hindi sentiment. Crediting Prime Minister Narendra Modi with lifting around 50 crore people out of poverty in 15 years, Radhakrishnan compared him to Abraham Lincoln as a nationalist.
items.title: Vice-President Radhakrishnan Urges National Unity for Cultural Preservation

items.summary: The Santa Ynez oil project operated by Sable Offshore has struggled to restart after a decade of shutdowns, with federal intervention under the Trump administration helping reopen its pipeline route. Production restarted from Harmony in May 2025, though California disputed this as well testing. The company disclosed that sole customer Chevron stopped purchases due to refinery maintenance, prompting shares to fall by more than half on November 9, reaching a record low of 76 cents at one point.
items.title: Sable Offshore Faces Uncertain Buyers Amid California Refinery Closures
